original.target_description: Study 1 recognition accuracy: target gender × orientation interaction in a mixed ANOVA including participant gender; sexualized male and female bodies only, with no object stimuli.

n.exclusions: No exclusions documented; 78 recruited but the printed interaction denominator df is 75, while paired tests have df 77. Analytic n for this interaction cannot be established without resolving this discrepancy.
n.location: p. 469 Method; p. 470 Results (repository PDF pp. 2–3)
n.quote: Seventy-eight university students (41 men, 37 women; [...] F(1, 75) = 15.07

replication.target_description: Study 2, original non-counterbalanced stimulus subset (Figure 2A): stimulus gender × orientation interaction in mixed ANOVA including participant gender; no object-control stimuli.

n.exclusions: No exclusions reported; 60 recruited, ANOVA denominator df 58 with two participant-gender groups, paired post hoc df 59.
n.location: accepted manuscript p. 12 Method; p. 13 Results
n.quote: Sixty adults (50% women, mean age 34.5 years, SD = 13.4, range from 19 to 69 [...] F(1, 58) = 10.48

reported_success.location: Study 2, Results and Discussion; accepted manuscript pp. 13, 18
reported_success.quote: Replicating Bernard et al. (2012), the critical interaction effect of Stimulus Gender and Stimulus Orientation was significant [...] the original results from Bernard et al. (2012) are based on stimulus subsets effects that are highly likely to be symmetry-confounds

notes: Titles verified against references. Target_match false because supplied description explicitly includes objects, absent from both located tests. Extracted closest identifiable interaction without merging controlled-design tests. Replication locator p.5 corresponds to published results; accepted-manuscript pagination differs. Replication full counterbalanced analysis reports the focal two-way interaction F < 1 and no exact p or eta-squared; this is a separate test (manuscript p.15). Success refers to original-setup statistical replication with authors' methodological caveat, not overall validation of sexual objectification.
